# dsh-publish-github
A **GitHub publishing plugin** for DeepSeek Harness: type one command in the composer and publish an
y local directory as a GitHub repository — `git init`, repo creation, commit and push, without leavi
ry as a GitHub repository — `git init`, repo creation, commit and push, without leaving the session.
## What it does
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One command covers the whole flow, reporting each step as a ✓/✗ line in the session.
## Why a slash command instead of a model tool
DSH's `@deepseek-ai/*` packages live inside the Electron `app.asar`, so a plugin mounted from disk *
*cannot import them** — which rules out the official `ctx.tools.register` path. This plugin register
s `/publish` through the host's `ctx.commands.register` instead, needing no internal package and wor
king as soon as it is mounted.

Alternatively, save `GITHUB_TOKEN` in DSH credentials — the plugin injects it as `GH_TOKEN` into the
`gh` child process, so gh's own login is not required.

## Safety

- **Never** force-pushes, deletes branches or resets history — such words are refused up front;
- Wh

en `origin` already exists it only performs a normal `push` and never recreates the remote;
- The ch

ild environment strips `DSH_*` variables so harness configuration never reaches `gh`;
- Any director
y is allowed (deliberate: the path the user names is the authorization).
## Requirements
| Dependency | Notes |

| `git` | required |
| `gh` | required (macOS `brew install gh` / Windows `winget install GitHub.cli

` / Linux `apt install gh`) |
| GitHub auth | `gh auth login`, or a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in DSH credential
## Known limitations
- Only the `/publish` command; there is no settings page (account details come from gh CLI or DSH cr

dsh@localhost>` (amend it afterwards if you prefer);
- No conflict handling: if the remote already h
as unrelated history, the push fails and the error is reported verbatim.
## Compatibility
| Item | Status |
| DSH version | Verified on `0.2.2-rc.1`; declares `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`; DSH rejects

an incompatible host at install time |
| Platform | Tested on macOS; **Windows untested**, with thr
ee adaptations in place: `gh`/`gh.exe`/`gh.cmd`/`gh.bat` are probed in order, arguments honour quote

s (including backslash paths), and the commit author is configurable |
| npm dependencies | **None**

: only `node:*` built-ins, no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports |
| Browser module dependencies | **None**: h

ost-only plugin, no client half |
| Required external tools | `git` and `gh`, both on `PATH` |
| Ins
tall | Declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` registers it as a profile layer automatically — no
manual patch editing |
> **After a DSH upgrade the plugin may refuse to install**: `engines.dsh` is enforced by DSH, which
rejects an out-of-window host and explains that running it may crash or corrupt data. To try an unve

rified host anyway, use DSH's exact-version exemption:
>
[代码示例省略，未执行]

>
> Back up your workspace first. The host APIs this plugin relies on (`ctx.commands.register`, the
right-sidebar tabs, `agents.create`'s seed semantics) can still change between release candidates.
Install verification: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucyVan/dsh-publish-github` was run in an
isolated `DSH_HOME`.
